scope.population_rule: the exact identity complement of the prior 16-row fixed sample within all CAND_unresolved_magnitude and CAND_same_turn_stat_event_gap rows
scope.sampling_method: census: adjudicate every remaining identity; no further sampling or replacement

disclosure: These predictions use only committed C14 family/class/basis strings and the already-committed 16-row C15 findings. No retained repro, branch instruction, engine roll, protocol ordering, or source locus for these 21 identities was inspected before this registration.

hypotheses.M1_legal_roll_matcher_accounting: The observed component is inside the engine's exact legal roll set, but the comparison path rejects it because it uses a representative roll or a non-event-aware set.
hypotheses.M2_switch_boundary_comparison_limit: The row crosses a switch boundary, so pre-state calculate_damage legality is not evidence for the post-switch hit; the row remains WHAT unless the retained branch state licenses a post-switch roll set.
hypotheses.M3_dynamic_state_timing: A damage-dependent fact such as HP, type, weather, status, or ability activation is read at the wrong point in the engine branch; a controlled one-fact replay should identify the exact timing locus.
hypotheses.M4_capped_or_inherited_residual: The mismatch is inherited from a capped or residual component whose represented value is not a freely roll-scaled damage component.
hypotheses.M5_static_engine_base_candidate: The observed value is outside the engine's exact legal roll set with no demonstrated dynamic timing cause. This remains WHAT-level unless branch/source reads identify an exact pipeline locus.
hypotheses.S1_event_aware_legal_set: A same-turn stat event is applied before damage in the engine branch and the observed value enters the post-event legal set, making this a comparison-instrument omission.
hypotheses.S2_post_event_base_discrepancy: The engine applies the same-turn event before damage, but the observed value remains outside the post-event legal set. This is an engine candidate but remains WHAT without an exact source locus.
hypotheses.S3_noncausal_or_misbucketed_event: The cited event occurs after the hit, affects the wrong battler/stat, or is unrelated to the mismatched component; the family label is not the WHY.

controls: Replay each retained repro first and read raw protocol order plus raw engine branch instructions before assigning a mechanism.
Enumerate calculate_damage legal rolls for the retained candidate state and both critical modes where legal; use membership, never roll-count similarity.
Do not use a pre-switch legal set to adjudicate damage after a switch. Require a retained post-switch state or leave the magnitude WHAT-level.
For same-turn events, compare pre-event and branch-applied post-event legal sets and inspect instruction ordering before calling either an engine phase defect or an instrument omission.
Run a controlled one-fact counterfactual only when the retained branch exposes a unique state anchor; record the changed fact and preserve all other state.
Check each row and its game for overlap with patches 42-44 and active world lanes; shared games do not imply shared row mechanisms.
Generalize only when every member of a proposed sub-shape supports the same WHY. Otherwise preserve row-level verdicts or WHAT status.
Do not implement engine fixes in this lane. Bank exact source/patch loci for a follow-up lane only after replay and source evidence agree.

scoring_rule.confirmed: the first listed expected mechanism is established by replay plus its registered discriminator
scoring_rule.partial: one of the listed expected mechanisms is supported, but the row remains WHAT-level or the exact source locus is not licensed
scoring_rule.refuted: none of the listed expected mechanisms explains the retained row
